newsitem.title: USA: Johnstown America hurt by weak demand.
newsitem.headline: Johnstown America hurt by weak demand.

text.p: Johnstown America Industries Inc said Wednesday its 1996 results were hurt by a decline in demand for railroad freight cars, and improvement will require an unturn in that market.
The manufacturer reported a fourth-quarter loss of $0.19 a share and a full-year loss of $0.55 a share on lower sales in both periods.
"Results were impacted by a sharp decline in demand for railroad cars," said chairman Thomas Bengel in a statement.

Bengel said the company's truck components and iron castings operations performed well in both periods despite somewhat softer market conditions in 1996, as did its freight car rebuilding and repair operation and railcar leasing subsidiary.
"Significant improvement, however, in our financial performance will require recovery of key segments of the freight car market," Bengel noted.

Johnstown said it ended the year with $24.5 million in cash, $12.9 million more than at the end of 1995. It said $25 million of debt was retired during the year, and there were no outstanding borrowings under its $100 million revolving credit facility at year-end.
